* business forms in PDF format or Microsoft Word

proposed:
Sensible is a developer-first platform for PDF data extraction and intelligent document processing: it extracts structured data from documents (also called document parsing) and returns it as JSON. This overview introduces SenseML, Sensible's extraction query language, its JSON output, and Sensible's DevOps platform, so you can decide how to use Sensible to build document-automation features into your vertical SaaS products. Sensible extracts data from documents such as:

* business forms in PDF format or Microsoft Word
* email bodies and attachments
* spreadsheets
* PNGs and JPEGs of documents

For data extracted by large language models (LLMs), Sensible asks the LLMs to report any uncertainties about the accuracy of the extracted data. For example, an LLM can report "multiple possible answers" or "ambiguous query".  These confidence *signals* offer more nuanced troubleshooting than numeric confidence *scores*.

Note that LLMs can inaccurately report confidence signals.  For more information about confidence signals, see the research paper [Teaching models to express their uncertainties in words](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.14334.pdf). 

Sensible support confidence signals for the Query Group method.

For more information about troubleshooting confidence signals, see the following table.
proposed:
LLM confidence signals are messages that a large language model (LLM) returns when it's uncertain about the accuracy of the data it extracted, for example, "multiple possible answers" or "ambiguous query." These confidence *signals* offer more nuanced troubleshooting than numeric confidence *scores*. Sensible supports confidence signals for the [Query Group](doc:query-group) method. This page lists each signal with its JSON output and tips, so you can spot uncertain extractions and troubleshoot them to improve extraction accuracy.

Note that LLMs can inaccurately report confidence signals. For more information about confidence signals, see the research paper [Teaching models to express their uncertainties in words](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.14334.pdf).

For asynchronous extractions, you can retrieve extraction results using either API endpoints or a webhook. A webhook allows you to receive the extraction as a push when its status changes, rather than polling the `/documents/{id}` API endpoint for extraction status. For example, if you set a webhook, you get a push when the extraction status changes to `COMPLETE`  or when the [review](doc:human-review) status changes to `APPROVED`.

For this tutorial, let's try a webhook in combination with the `/extract_from_url` endpoint. Note you can also use a webhook with any other extraction endpoint.
proposed: A Sensible webhook pushes asynchronous extraction results to a URL you specify when an extraction's status changes, so you don't have to poll the `/documents/{id}` API endpoint. For example, you get a push when the extraction status changes to `COMPLETE` or when the [review](doc:human-review) status changes to `APPROVED`. In this tutorial, you add a webhook to an `/extract_from_url` request for an example tax form, then inspect the pushed payload at a test URL. You can use the same approach with any other extraction endpoint.

replaces:
JsonLogic is a library for processing rules written in JSON. A JsonLogic rule is structured as follows: `{ "operator" : ["values" ... ] }`.  For example, `{ "cat" : ["I love", "pie"] }` results in `"I love pie"`.

Sensible supports both built-in and extended JsonLogic operators so that you can transform and validate extracted document data.
proposed: JsonLogic is a JSON rules engine: a library for processing rules structured as `{ "operator" : ["values" ... ] }`. For example, `{ "cat" : ["I love", "pie"] }` results in `"I love pie"`. This page is the reference for Sensible's custom JsonLogic operators, such as Date Shift, Match, and Pick Fields, with syntax tips and examples, so you can write rules that transform and validate extracted data in validations, Custom Computation methods, or postprocessors. Sensible also supports the built-in and extended JsonLogic operators described in the following documentation.
rationale: Keeps the JsonLogic definition but adds that the page is the reference for Sensible's custom operators and where they apply (fixes A and D); the external-docs link list stays in place because restructuring is out of scope. This page describes the Field object's top-level parameters, such as Anchor, Method, and Type, and shows example fields, so you can define fields in your config.
